body.statement:
For the inductive shared-trace extension there is an input-computable integer \(C_{\mathfrak G}\ge1\) such that, for rational \(L,B\ge1\), the rational cutoffs, the subordinate partition of unity, the incidence forest, and protected neighborhoods can be chosen so that all chart traces agree exactly on simultaneous supports and, for every \(f:\mathcal A\to[0,R_f]\),
\[
 \sum_{\tau\prec\sigma}\int
 \|\nabla\chi_{\tau\sigma}(w)\|_{\Sigma}
 |F_\sigma^f(w)-F_\tau^f(w)|\phi_\Sigma(w-h)\,dw
 \le \frac{C_{\mathfrak G}R_f}{L},
\]
and, on every declared coverage or separated-risk mean cell,
\[
 \sum_e\Gamma_{C,e}^f+\frac{R_f}{2}\omega(h)
 \le C_{\mathfrak G}R_f
 \left(\frac{d}{L}+\frac{d}{B^2}\right).
\]
Both inequalities are uniform in \(h\), including means centered on an incidence seam, and do not require the incident cone-interior candidates to be close.
body.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: exact trace induction plus slow-cutoff variation, rather than convergence of independently averaged charts.}

On a rational collar coordinate \(a\), begin with the piecewise-linear cutoff
\[
 \chi_L(a)=
 \begin{cases}
 0,&a\le0,\\
 a/L,&0<a<L,\\
 1,&a\ge L.
 \end{cases}
\tag{16}
\]
If the dual Mahalanobis norm of the rational collar coordinate is \(c_a\), replace the physical collar length by \(c_aL\).  Then \(\|\nabla\chi_L\|_\Sigma\le L^{-1}\).  The barycentric subdivision has a computable overlap number and every incidence path has length at most its finite dimension.  Let \(C_{\mathfrak G}\) dominate the sum of these finitely many overlap and path constants.

Because \(0\le F_\alpha^f\le R_f\),
\[
 \int \|\nabla\chi_{\tau\sigma}(w)\|_\Sigma
 |F_\sigma^f(w)-F_\tau^f(w)|\phi_\Sigma(w-h)\,dw
 \le \frac{R_f}{L}.
\tag{17}
\]
Summing (17) over the bounded number of active collars proves the first displayed inequality.  Notice that only boundedness was used; the endpoint discrepancy may equal \(R_f\).

The dimension induction in \(\mathrm{def:inductive\mbox{-}shared\mbox{-}trace\mbox{-}extension}\) copies, rather than recomputes, a lower-skeleton rule.  Thus two incident chart restrictions are identical wherever their partition weights are simultaneously positive.  This remains true at a branching intersection because the induction has a single already-constructed value there.  For a mean cell \(C\), choose as anchor its deepest active stratum and route every other active chart along the barycentric parent path.  Take \(P_{C,e}\) to contain the guarded star on which the two endpoint restrictions are identical.  On this set the first integrand in \(\Gamma_{C,e}^f\) is zero whenever the corresponding path load is locally active.

The remaining path load has one of two causes.  Either its chart has zero weight at \(h\), or the observation crossed the guard of width \(B\).  In the first case it is bounded by the total weight variation.  Since the sum of the dual Mahalanobis Lipschitz constants of the partition is at most \(C_{\mathfrak G}/L\), writing \(W=h+\Sigma^{1/2}Z\), with \(Z\sim N_d(0,I_d)\), gives
\[
 \omega(h)
 \le \frac{C_{\mathfrak G}}{L}E\|Z\|_2
 \le \frac{C_{\mathfrak G}d}{L}.
\tag{18}
\]
In the second case, Markov's inequality applied to \(\|Z\|_2^2\), whose expectation is \(d\), gives
\[
 P_h\{\|W-h\|_{\Sigma^{-1}}>B\}
 \le \frac{d}{B^2}.
\tag{19}
\]
Multiplying (18)--(19) by \(R_f\), and then by the computably bounded path multiplicity, bounds both the protected-set integral and the complement term in every \(\Gamma_{C,e}^f\).  Enlarging \(C_{\mathfrak G}\) once proves the second displayed inequality.  Exact traces, not a small endpoint difference, cover seam-centered means.  This proves the lemma.
body.justification: Exact traces eliminate local branching discrepancies, while slowly varying weights and guarded tails control the remaining data-dependent selection uniformly in translated means.
body.gap: Closed without requiring incident endpoint rules to approach one another.
body.consumer: The shared-extension preservation lemma and effective compatible-density theorem use its uniform ledger bound.
